name: Terminal Relative Components Have at Least Nine Vertices
statement: Let $K\subsetneq A$ be ample and put $D=A\setminus K$. If $K\cup\{d\}$ is nonample for every $d\in D$, then every connected component of the graph induced by $D$ has at least nine vertices. In particular, when $|D|\le17$, the residual graph is connected.
proof: The relative Alexander-dual Yang module has a linear presentation whose annihilator and edge relations never cross residual components. It therefore splits as a direct sum over the components, and each summand has a linear resolution. The corresponding exact sequence makes $K$ together with any one component ample. If a component had at most eight concepts, the relative linear-quotient theorem through eight facets would order it with a first concept that can be adjoined amply to $K$, contradicting terminality. Two components therefore require at least eighteen concepts.
